question: The practice in the Parliament where the demands for grants are put to a vote after the passage of the time limit for discussion is called ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is guillotine.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The guillotine (गिलोटिन) is a parliamentary device by which the Speaker, on the last allotted day for the Demands for Grants, puts all the outstanding demands to vote at once after the time fixed for discussion has expired.

• It ensures that the Budget (Appropriation Bill) is passed within the stipulated time schedule of the House.

• Undiscussed demands are thus 'guillotined' and voted upon without debate.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The financial business of the House is completed within a fixed calendar under Rules of Procedure.

• The Demands for Grants are presented ministry-wise and voted only by the Lok Sabha.

• Rajya Sabha can only discuss the Budget, it cannot vote on Demands for Grants.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): Cut motions are motions moved to reduce the amount of a demand for grant (Policy Cut, Economy Cut, Token Cut), not the time-limit voting practice.

• opt (Option 3): 'Motions' is a general term for any proposal moved in the House and does not denote this specific practice.

• opt (Option 4): A point of order is raised to draw attention to a breach of rules or procedure, unrelated to voting of grants.

question: Which Indian city is known for its abundance of buildings featuring French colonial architecture?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Puducherry (Pondicherry).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Puducherry (पुडुचेरी) was a French colony (French India) for nearly 280 years until 1954 and retains a strong French architectural heritage.

• Its 'White Town' (Ville Blanche) is famous for French-style villas, wide boulevards, colonial mansions and the French Quarter.

• The city still preserves French street names, cafés and the influence of French urban planning.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Puducherry became a Union Territory of India in 1962 after de facto transfer in 1954.

• It comprises four regions: Puducherry, Karaikal, Yanam and Mahe.

• Auroville, the experimental township, is located near Puducherry.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Goa is known for Portuguese colonial architecture, not French.

• opt (Option 3): Hyderabad is noted for Indo-Islamic (Qutb Shahi/Nizam) architecture like the Charminar.

• opt (Option 4): Kolkata is associated with British colonial architecture.

question: Which French author was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2022 for her courage and clinical acuity in uncovering personal memory?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Annie Ernaux.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Annie Ernaux (एनी एरनॉक्स) won the 2022 Nobel Prize in Literature 'for the courage and clinical acuity with which she uncovers the roots, estrangements and collective restraints of personal memory'.

• She is a French author known for autobiographical works blending memoir and sociology.

• Notable works include 'The Years' (Les Années) and 'A Man's Place'.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• She was the first French woman to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature.

• Her writing style is often described as 'flat writing' (écriture plate).

• The Nobel Prize in Literature is awarded by the Swedish Academy.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): Leila Slimani is a French-Moroccan author who won the Prix Goncourt (2016), not the Nobel.

• opt (Option 3): Marie NDiaye is a French writer and Prix Goncourt winner (2009), but not the 2022 Nobel laureate.

• opt (Option 4): Delphine de Vigan is a French novelist, not a Nobel laureate.

question: The David Dixon Award is presented at the Commonwealth Games to whom?
option_3: The team with the best sportsmanship
solution_text:
The correct answer is The best athlete.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The David Dixon Award (डेविड डिक्सन पुरस्कार) is presented to the outstanding/best athlete of a Commonwealth Games edition.

• It is named after David Dixon, a former Honorary Secretary/CEO of the Commonwealth Games Federation.

• The winner is selected considering performance as well as fair play and conduct during the Games.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The award was first presented at the 2002 Manchester Commonwealth Games.

• The Commonwealth Games are held every four years and organised by the Commonwealth Games Federation (CGF).

• India has hosted the Commonwealth Games once, in Delhi in 2010.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): No single 'David Dixon Award' is given to the overall winning nation; the medal tally decides national rankings.

• opt (Option 3): Best sportsmanship of a team is not the criterion of this individual award.

• opt (Option 4): The host city is not recognised by this award.

question: The introduction of the Permanent Settlement in Bengal by Lord Cornwallis in 1793 primarily aimed to:
option_1: Ensure the welfare of the peasant farmers.
option_2: Create a class of loyal zamindars who would ensure regular land revenue collection.
option_3: Promote the cultivation of cash crops like indigo and cotton.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Create a class of loyal zamindars who would ensure regular land revenue collection.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Permanent Settlement (स्थायी बंदोबस्त) of 1793 fixed land revenue permanently and made zamindars the proprietors of land.

• Its primary aim was to create a stable, loyal class of zamindars who would guarantee a fixed and regular flow of land revenue to the Company.

• It was introduced by Lord Cornwallis in Bengal, Bihar and Odisha.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The system was based on the recommendations of John Shore.

• Zamindars had to deposit revenue by a fixed date (Sunset Law), failing which their estates were auctioned.

• The actual cultivators (ryots) were reduced to tenants with little security.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Peasant welfare was not the aim; peasants suffered heavily under the system.

• opt (Option 3): Promotion of cash crops was not the primary objective of the settlement.

• opt (Option 4): It entrenched, rather than abolished, the zamindari system.

question: One of the key technological shifts in the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) includes the introduction of which of the following systems?
option_3: Virtual trial-only courts for all offenses
solution_text:
The correct answer is e-FIR, e-summons and e-warrants.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (भारतीय नागरिक सुरक्षा संहिता) promotes digitisation of the criminal justice process, including e-FIR, electronic service of summons and warrants.

• It emphasises the use of technology, audio-video electronic means and digital records in investigation and trial.

• The BNSS replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973, with effect from 1 July 2024.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The three new criminal laws are BNS, BNSS and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA).

• BNSS mandates forensic investigation for offences punishable with seven years or more imprisonment.

• It fixes timelines for various stages of investigation and trial for speedy justice.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): BNSS does not introduce an 'AI-based trial judgment generator'; judgments are delivered by courts.

• opt (Option 2): 'Drone-based crime scene scanning' is not a provision introduced by the BNSS.

• opt (Option 3): Trials are not made 'virtual-only for all offenses'; physical proceedings continue with electronic support.

question: Which two basic postures form the foundation of Odissi dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chowk and Tribhanga.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chowk and Tribhanga (चौक और त्रिभंग) are the two fundamental postures/stances of Odissi dance.

• Chowk is a symmetrical, square-like wide stance symbolising Lord Jagannath, while Tribhanga is a graceful three-bend posture of the body.

• Odissi is a classical dance form of Odisha.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Odissi is one of the eight recognised classical dance forms of India.

• It has temple origins linked to the Maharis (devadasis) and Gotipuas.

• Famous exponents include Kelucharan Mohapatra and Sanjukta Panigrahi.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Tandava and Lasya are the vigorous (masculine) and graceful (feminine) aspects of dance in general, not the basic postures of Odissi.

• opt (Option 3): Chakkar (spins) and Mudra (hand gestures) are elements of dance but not the foundational stances of Odissi.

• opt (Option 4): Natya and Nritya are broad categories of dance/drama, not Odissi postures.

question: The life-size standing image of Yakshini holding a chauri (flywhisk) is an example of the sculptural tradition of which period?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mauryan Period.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous life-size Didarganj Yakshini (मौर्य काल) holding a chauri (flywhisk) is a masterpiece of the Mauryan period sculptural tradition.

• It is renowned for its highly polished, lustrous Mauryan (Chunar sandstone) finish.

• The image was discovered near Didarganj, Patna (Bihar).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The characteristic mirror-like Mauryan polish is a hallmark of the period's stone art.

• Ashokan pillars and their animal capitals also belong to the Mauryan sculptural tradition.

• The Lion Capital of Sarnath is India's National Emblem.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): Gupta period sculpture is later and known for classical images like the Sarnath Buddha, not the Didarganj Yakshini.

• opt (Option 3): Kushan period is associated with Gandhara and Mathura schools of art.

• opt (Option 4): Sunga period art is seen in Bharhut and early Sanchi railings, of a different style.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are true?
Statement 1: The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram exemplifies Dravidian architecture built of carved granite blocks.
Statement 2: This temple showcases architectural continuity from the Pallava-era rock-cut cave temples to fully structural stone constructions.
option_1: Both statements are true, and Statement 2 is the correct explanation of Statement 1.
option_2: Both statements are correct, but Statement 2 is not the correct explanation of Statement 1.
option_3: Statement 1 is correct, Statement 2 is false.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both statements are true, and Statement 2 is the correct explanation of Statement 1.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram (महाबलीपुरम का तट मंदिर) is a structural temple built of carved granite blocks in the Dravidian style.

• It marks the transition of Pallava architecture from rock-cut cave temples and monolithic rathas to fully structural stone temples.

• Hence Statement 2 correctly explains why the temple (Statement 1) represents Dravidian structural architecture.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• It was built during the reign of the Pallava king Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha).

• Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram) is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Tamil Nadu.

• Other monuments there include the Pancha Rathas and the Arjuna's Penance relief.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): Incorrect because Statement 2 IS the correct explanation of Statement 1.

• opt (Option 3): Incorrect because Statement 2 is true, not false.

• opt (Option 4): Incorrect because both statements are indeed true.

question: Wangala Festival is associated with which of the following tribe of India?
option_3: Balti tribes of Jammu and Kashmir
solution_text:
The correct answer is Garo tribe of Meghalaya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Wangala festival (गारो जनजाति) is celebrated by the Garo tribe of Meghalaya.

• It is a post-harvest festival honouring Saljong, the sun-god of fertility.

• It is also known as the 'Hundred Drums Festival' due to the synchronised drumming.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Garo are one of the major matrilineal tribes of Meghalaya, along with the Khasi and Jaintia.

• Wangala is usually celebrated in November.

• Meghalaya's capital is Shillong.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): The Bhotia tribes of Uttarakhand are not associated with Wangala.

• opt (Option 3): The Balti tribes of Jammu and Kashmir are not linked to this festival.

• opt (Option 4): The Nyishi of Arunachal Pradesh celebrate festivals like Nyokum, not Wangala.

question: How is the Rigveda best described in the context of ancient Indian literature?
option_4: A collection of hymns across ages
solution_text:
The correct answer is A collection of hymns across ages.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Rigveda (ऋग्वेद) is the oldest Veda and is essentially a collection of hymns (suktas) in praise of various deities.

• It is composed of mantras arranged in ten mandalas (books).

• It is the oldest known text of the Indo-Aryan tradition.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Gayatri Mantra is found in the Rigveda (Mandala 3, dedicated to sage Vishwamitra).

• The four Vedas are Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda and Atharvaveda.

• 'Satyameva Jayate' is taken from the Mundaka Upanishad.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): The Upanishads are later philosophical texts (Vedanta), not what the Rigveda is a compilation of.

• opt (Option 2): The Samaveda, not the Rigveda, is chiefly linked to musical chanting.

• opt (Option 3): The Rigveda is not a collection of royal chronicles.

question:
Which of the following statements about Kho-Kho rules is/are correct?
1) Pole height is 1.20-1.25 m with a fixed 9 cm diameter.
2) Total match duration including intervals is 48 minutes.
3) Sub-junior chasers' block distance is same as juniors: 2.30 m.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 2 is Correct.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In Kho-Kho (खो-खो), the total match duration including the intervals is 48 minutes, making Statement 2 correct.

• The standard pole height is 120-125 cm but its diameter is not fixed at 9 cm (it ranges around 9-10 cm), so Statement 1 is not fully correct.

• The block distance for sub-juniors differs from that of juniors, so Statement 3 is incorrect.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Kho-Kho is a traditional Indian tag-and-chase sport played between two teams.

• A team consists of twelve players, of whom nine take the field.

• The Ultimate Kho Kho league was launched in India in 2022.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Only Statement 1 being correct is wrong, as the fixed 9 cm diameter claim is inaccurate.

• opt (Option 3): Only Statement 3 being correct is wrong, as sub-junior block distance differs from juniors.

• opt (Option 4): All three being correct is wrong since Statements 1 and 3 are inaccurate.

question: What does the term "Kunbis" refer to in the context of Maratha society?
option_1: A warrior caste of the Rajput clans
solution_text:
The correct answer is A group of peasant-pastoralists.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In Maratha society, the Kunbis (कुनबी) were a group of peasant-pastoralists / agriculturists who formed the backbone of the rural economy.

• Many low-ranking Maratha soldiers and cultivators came from the Kunbi community.

• The terms 'Maratha' and 'Kunbi' were closely connected, with Kunbis engaged in farming and cattle-rearing.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Marathas rose to power in the 17th century under Chhatrapati Shivaji.

• Agriculture and peasant militias were central to the Maratha state.

• The Deccan region was the heartland of Maratha society.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Kunbis were not a warrior caste of the Rajput clans.

• opt (Option 2): They were cultivators, not a class of temple priests.

• opt (Option 4): They were not a community of merchant bankers.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding athlete responsibilities in anti-doping procedures:
1) Athletes must provide accurate whereabouts information and comply with all sample collection procedures.
2) Athletes are allowed to delegate the sample collection process to a team official if they have a valid reason.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1 is Correct.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under anti-doping rules, athletes must provide accurate whereabouts information (ठिकाने की जानकारी) and comply with all sample collection procedures, so Statement 1 is correct.

• Sample collection is a personal responsibility of the athlete and cannot be delegated to a team official, so Statement 2 is incorrect.

• The provision of a urine/blood sample must be witnessed and completed by the athlete themselves.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Anti-doping in India is governed by the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA).

• The World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) sets global anti-doping standards.

• The National Anti-Doping Act, 2022 gave statutory status to NADA in India.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): Delegating sample collection is not permitted, so 'Only 2 correct' is wrong.

• opt (Option 3): Both cannot be correct because Statement 2 is false.

• opt (Option 4): 'Neither correct' is wrong because Statement 1 is valid.

question: 'Why Nations Fail' is co-authored by Daron Acemoglu and________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is James Robinson.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Why Nations Fail' (2012) is co-authored by Daron Acemoglu and James Robinson (जेम्स रॉबिन्सन).

• The book argues that inclusive political and economic institutions drive prosperity, while extractive institutions lead to failure.

• Both authors were awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences in 2024 (along with Simon Johnson).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Acemoglu and Robinson also co-wrote 'The Narrow Corridor'.

• The 2024 Economics Nobel recognised work on how institutions shape national prosperity.

• James Robinson is a political scientist and economist at the University of Chicago.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Fareed Zakaria is a journalist and author (e.g. 'The Post-American World'), not a co-author of this book.

• opt (Option 2): Abhijit Banerjee co-authored 'Poor Economics', not 'Why Nations Fail'.

• opt (Option 4): Raghuram Rajan wrote 'Fault Lines' and 'I Do What I Do', not this book.

question:
Consider the following statements about Khelo India Winter Games 2024:
1.) Indian Army topped the medal tally with 10 golds.
2.) Jammu & Kashmir, former champions, finished second in 2024 with nine gold medals.
Which of the following Statement is/are Correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1 is correct.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At the Khelo India Winter Games 2024 (खेलो इंडिया शीतकालीन खेल), the Indian Army topped the medal tally, making Statement 1 correct.

• Jammu & Kashmir did not finish second with nine golds in 2024 (the runner-up position and figures in Statement 2 do not match), so Statement 2 is incorrect.

• The Games were held at Gulmarg and Leh.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Khelo India Winter Games are held to promote winter sports in India.

• Events include skiing, snowboarding, ice hockey and ice skating.

• The Khelo India programme was launched by the Government of India in 2018.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): Statement 2 is inaccurate, so 'Only 2 correct' is wrong.

• opt (Option 3): Both cannot be correct because Statement 2 is wrong.

• opt (Option 4): 'Neither correct' is wrong because Statement 1 is valid.

question: Which Constitutional Amendment made it mandatory for States to establish Panchayati Raj Institutions as units of local self-governance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 73rd Amendment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 (73वां संशोधन) gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions.

• It added Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution and made establishment of Panchayats mandatory.

• It provided for a three-tier structure of Panchayats at village, intermediate and district levels.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• It came into force on 24 April 1993, celebrated as National Panchayati Raj Day.

• It provides for reservation of seats for SCs, STs and women (not less than one-third).

• Article 40 (DPSP) had earlier called for the organisation of village panchayats.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): The 42nd Amendment (1976) is the 'Mini-Constitution' and added words like Socialist, Secular; it did not mandate Panchayati Raj.

• opt (Option 2): The 74th Amendment deals with urban local bodies (Municipalities), not Panchayats.

• opt (Option 4): The 44th Amendment (1978) removed the Right to Property as a Fundamental Right, unrelated to Panchayats.

question: A person needs spectacles with a power of -2.5 D. This indicates that the person is suffering from:
option_1: Hypermetropia (farsightedness) and needs a converging lens.
option_2: Myopia (nearsightedness) and needs a diverging lens.
option_3: Presbyopia and needs a bifocal lens.
option_4: Astigmatism and needs a cylindrical lens.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Myopia (nearsightedness) and needs a diverging lens.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A negative lens power (-2.5 D) denotes a concave (diverging) lens, which is used to correct myopia (मायोपिया / निकट दृष्टिदोष).

• In myopia, distant objects appear blurred because the image is formed in front of the retina.

• A concave (diverging) lens shifts the image back onto the retina, correcting the defect.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Power of a lens P = 1/f (in metres), and the SI unit of power is dioptre (D).

• Myopia is caused by elongation of the eyeball or excessive curvature of the cornea/lens.

• Hypermetropia (far-sightedness) is corrected using convex (converging, positive power) lenses.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Hypermetropia requires a convex lens of positive power, not a negative power lens.

• opt (Option 3): Presbyopia (age-related) is corrected using bifocal lenses, not simply -2.5 D.

• opt (Option 4): Astigmatism is corrected using cylindrical lenses and is a different defect.

question: Which of the following statements correctly describes modern currency systems?
option_1: Currencies are fully backed by gold
option_2: Currencies are not readily convertible into gold
option_3: Currencies can always be exchanged for barrels of oil
solution_text:
The correct answer is Currencies are not readily convertible into gold.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Modern currencies are fiat money (मुद्राएँ आसानी से सोने में परिवर्तित नहीं की जा सकतीं) — they are not freely convertible into gold.

• Their value rests on government backing and public trust, not on a fixed gold reserve.

• The gold standard was abandoned by most countries during the 20th century.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The end of the Bretton Woods system in 1971 ('Nixon Shock') marked the move away from gold convertibility.

• Fiat currency derives value from legal tender status and central bank management.

• In India, currency is issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Modern currencies are not fully backed by gold under fiat systems.

• opt (Option 3): Currencies are not fixed for exchange into barrels of oil.

• opt (Option 4): Currencies are not backed by silver in modern systems.

question: The Green Revolution in India was introduced during which plan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Third.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Green Revolution (हरित क्रांति) in India was introduced during the Third Five Year Plan period (in the mid-1960s).

• It involved the use of High-Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilisers, irrigation and modern farm technology.

• It greatly boosted the production of wheat and rice, especially in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• M.S. Swaminathan is called the 'Father of the Green Revolution in India'.

• Norman Borlaug is regarded as the 'Father of the Green Revolution' worldwide.

• The programme made India self-sufficient in foodgrains.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): The Second Plan focused on rapid industrialisation (Mahalanobis model), not the Green Revolution.

• opt (Option 3): The Fourth Plan followed later and consolidated agricultural growth but did not introduce it.

• opt (Option 4): The Fifth Plan focused on poverty removal (Garibi Hatao) and self-reliance.

question: A higher ranking in the World Press Freedom Index indicates:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Greater journalistic freedom.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A higher (better) ranking in the World Press Freedom Index (विश्व प्रेस स्वतंत्रता सूचकांक) indicates greater journalistic freedom in a country.

• The Index is published annually by Reporters Without Borders (RSF).

• It evaluates media independence, safety of journalists, and the legal and political environment.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• A rank closer to 1 reflects a freer press; a lower rank reflects greater restrictions.

• The Index covers around 180 countries and territories.

• Scandinavian countries usually top the Index.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): More government control corresponds to a lower ranking, not a higher one.

• opt (Option 3): Increased censorship worsens the ranking.

• opt (Option 4): Lower public trust in media is not what a higher ranking measures.

question: Tana Bhagat led a unique tribal movement in the early 20th century, emphasizing reforms and non-violence against the British and local landlords among the Oraon community in which modern-day state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jharkhand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Tana Bhagat movement (झारखंड) was led among the Oraon tribal community in the Chotanagpur region of present-day Jharkhand.

• It began around 1914 under leaders like Jatra Bhagat, stressing reforms, monotheism and non-violence against the British and zamindars.

• The movement is noted for its early use of non-violent resistance and later alignment with the Gandhian freedom struggle.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Jatra Oraon (Jatra Bhagat) is regarded as the founder of the Tana Bhagat movement.

• The Tana Bhagats refused to pay taxes and boycotted British goods.

• Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar as a separate state in November 2000.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Chhattisgarh was not the centre of the Oraon Tana Bhagat movement.

• opt (Option 2): Madhya Pradesh is not associated with this movement.

• opt (Option 4): West Bengal is not the modern-day state of this movement's core area.

question: Which significant political move by Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi ensured that Assam remained a part of India and not East Pakistan during the Cabinet Mission Plan's proposal in 1946?
option_1: Opposing the grouping of Assam with Bengal
option_2: Launching the Quit India Movement in Assam
solution_text:
The correct answer is Opposing the grouping of Assam with Bengal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gopinath Bordoloi (असम को बंगाल के साथ समूहीकृत करने का विरोध) strongly opposed the Cabinet Mission Plan's proposal to group Assam with Muslim-majority Bengal (Group C).

• His resistance ensured that Assam did not become part of East Pakistan and remained with India.

• He was supported by Mahatma Gandhi in this stand.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Gopinath Bordoloi was the first Chief Minister of Assam.

• He was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1999.

• The Cabinet Mission (1946) proposed a grouping of provinces into Sections A, B and C.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): The Quit India Movement (1942) was nationwide and predates the 1946 Cabinet Mission issue.

• opt (Option 3): The Assam Accord was signed in 1985, long after Bordoloi's time.

• opt (Option 4): Rejecting an Instrument of Accession is unrelated to this decision on Assam.

question: Under which Five Year Plan was the Green Revolution introduced in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Third Plan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Green Revolution (हरित क्रांति) was introduced in India during the Third Five Year Plan period in the mid-1960s.

• It brought High-Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, fertilisers, pesticides and assured irrigation to Indian agriculture.

• It transformed India from a food-deficit to a food-surplus nation in wheat and rice.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Third Plan (1961-66) initially focused on making the economy self-reliant.

• M.S. Swaminathan is known as the 'Father of the Green Revolution in India'.

• The strategy is also called the 'New Agricultural Strategy'.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): The First Plan (1951-56) was based on the Harrod-Domar model and focused on agriculture and irrigation, not the Green Revolution.

• opt (Option 2): The Second Plan focused on heavy industrialisation.

• opt (Option 4): The Fourth Plan came later and consolidated agricultural gains but did not introduce it.

question: Which sector suffered due to reduction in fertilizer subsidies post-1991?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Agriculture.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The reduction in fertilizer subsidies (कृषि) after the 1991 economic reforms directly affected the agriculture sector.

• Higher input costs increased the burden on farmers, who depend heavily on subsidised fertilizers.

• Fertilizer subsidy is a key component of agricultural support in India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The 1991 reforms (LPG — Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation) aimed at cutting fiscal deficits, including subsidy cuts.

• Fertilizer subsidy is provided mainly on urea and nutrient-based fertilizers.
